definitions.en: a tool with a round end used for eating or mixing food

examples.en: She ate the soup with a spoon.

spoon.etymology: 源自古英语 spōn，意为“木片”。

definitions.en: a twisted piece of metal that jumps back when you press it
a place where water comes up from the ground

examples.en: The bed has a soft spring in it.
examples.cn: 这张床里有柔软的弹簧。

spring.etymology: 源自古英语 spring，意为“涌出之处”。

definitions.en: a flat shape with four equal sides and four right angles
an open area in a town with buildings around it

examples.en: The window is a perfect square.
examples.cn: 这扇窗户是个完美的正方形。

examples.en: We met in the town square.

square.etymology: 源自古法语 esquarre,源于拉丁语 exquadrare(使成方形),含 quattuor(四)。

synonyms.nuance: 多指城市中开阔的公共场所

definitions.en: a small piece of paper you put on a letter to send it
a tool used to print a mark, or the mark itself

examples.en: She put a stamp on the letter.
examples.cn: 她在信上贴了一张邮票。

examples.en: The man put his stamp on the paper.
examples.cn: 那个人在纸上盖了印章。

stamp.etymology: 源自中古英语 stampen,意为用脚踩、压印。

synonyms.nuance: 多指正式或官方的封印

definitions.en: a bright point of light in the night sky

examples.en: There is a bright star in the sky.
examples.cn: 天空中有一颗明亮的星星。

examples.en: We saw many stars at night.
examples.cn: 夜里我们看到了许多星星。

star.etymology: 源自古英语 steorra,与拉丁语 stella、希腊语 aster 同源。

definitions.en: a place where trains or buses stop for people to get on and off

examples.en: The train is at the station.
I will meet you at the station.

station.etymology: 源自拉丁语 statio(站立、驻地),含词根 sta-(站立)。

synonyms.nuance: 多指公交或路途中的小站

definitions.en: the long thin part of a plant that holds up the leaves and flowers

examples.en: The flower has a long stem.
She cut the stem of the rose.

stem.etymology: 源自古英语 stemn,意为树干、茎杆。

synonyms.nuance: 多指较硬的草本植物的茎

definitions.en: a thin piece of wood from a tree

examples.en: The dog ran after the stick.
He picked up some sticks for the fire.

stick.etymology: 源自古英语 sticca,意为小树枝、棍。

definitions.en: a piece of clothing that covers the foot and leg

examples.en: She put on a warm stocking.
examples.cn: 她穿上了一只暖和的长袜。

examples.en: The girl hung a stocking by the fire.
examples.cn: 那女孩在火炉旁挂了一只长袜。

stocking.etymology: 源自 stock 的旧义(覆盖腿脚的衣物)加 -ing。

synonyms.nuance: 指较短、只到脚踝的袜子

definitions.en: the part of the body where food goes after you eat

examples.en: My stomach hurts after the big meal.
He has a pain in his stomach.

stomach.etymology: 源自希腊语 stomachos,源于 stoma(口、开口)。

definitions.en: a place where you can buy things

examples.en: I bought some bread at the store.
The store opens at nine.

store.etymology: 源自古法语 estor,源于拉丁语 instaurare(储备)。

synonyms.nuance: 英式英语更常用,多指较小的店

definitions.en: a road in a town with houses or shops on its sides

examples.en: Children are playing in the street.
We walked down the busy street.
examples.cn: 我们沿着繁忙的街道走着。

street.etymology: 源自古英语 stræt,源于拉丁语 strata(铺好的路)。

definitions.en: the bright star in the sky that gives us light and heat

examples.en: The sun is bright today.
The sun comes up in the morning.

sun.etymology: 源自古英语 sunne,与拉丁语 sol 同源。

definitions.en: a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs

examples.en: The food is on the table.
We sat around the table.

table.etymology: 源自拉丁语 tabula(板、平面)。

synonyms.nuance: 多指供书写或工作的桌

definitions.en: the part at the back end of an animal's body

examples.en: The dog has a long tail.
The cat moved its tail slowly.
examples.cn: 那只猫慢慢地摆动尾巴。

tail.etymology: 源自古英语 tægel,意为动物的尾。

definitions.en: a long thin piece of cotton used for sewing

examples.en: She needs a needle and thread.
The thread is too thin to see.

thread.etymology: 源自古英语 thræd,与 throw(扭、纺)相关。

definitions.en: the front part of the neck, and the passage inside it

examples.en: I have a sore throat.
He drank water to wet his throat.

throat.etymology: 源自古英语 throte,与 throttle 同源。

definitions.en: the short thick finger on the side of your hand

examples.en: He hurt his thumb with the door.
She put up her thumb to say yes.

thumb.etymology: 源自古英语 thuma,意为粗短的指。

definitions.en: a small piece of paper that lets you travel or go in somewhere

examples.en: I bought a ticket for the train.
Please show your ticket at the gate.

ticket.etymology: 源自古法语 estiquet(标签),与 stick(贴、插)相关。

synonyms.nuance: 多指可反复使用的许可证

examples.en: I hurt my toe.

definitions.en: the soft part in your mouth that you use to taste and talk

examples.en: The dog put out its tongue.
I burned my tongue on the hot soup.

tongue.etymology: 源自古英语 tunge,与拉丁语 lingua 同源。

examples.en: Brush your teeth every day.

definitions.en: a place with houses, shops and streets, smaller than a city

examples.en: They live in a small town.
We went to town to buy food.

town.etymology: 源自古英语 tun,意为围地、村落。

definitions.en: a line of railway cars pulled by an engine

examples.en: The train came into the station.
We took a train to the city.

train.etymology: 源自古法语 train(拖、一连串),源于拉丁语 trahere(拉)。

definitions.en: a flat object used to carry food or drinks

examples.en: She carried the cups on a tray.
Put the cups back on the tray.

tray.etymology: 源自古英语 treg,意为木盘,与 tree(木)相关。

definitions.en: a tall plant with a trunk, branches and leaves

examples.en: A bird is in the tree.
There are many trees in the park.

tree.etymology: 源自古英语 treow,意为树、木。

definitions.en: a piece of clothing for the legs and lower body

examples.en: He is wearing blue trousers.
These trousers are too long for me.
examples.cn: 这条裤子对我来说太长了。

trousers.etymology: 源自盖尔语 triubhas(紧身裤),后受 drawers 影响加 -s。

definitions.en: a thing you hold over your head to keep off the rain

examples.en: Take an umbrella, it may rain.
She opened her umbrella in the rain.

umbrella.etymology: 源自意大利语 ombrella,源于拉丁语 umbra(影、阴)。

definitions.en: the side of a room or a building, or a high structure round a place

examples.en: There is a picture on the wall.
A high wall is around the garden.

wall.etymology: 源自古英语 weall,源于拉丁语 vallum(壁垒)。

definitions.en: a small clock that you wear on your wrist

examples.en: He looked at his watch.
My watch says it is three o'clock.
examples.cn: 我的手表显示是三点钟。

watch.etymology: 源自古英语 wæcce(守夜),后引申为计时器。

definitions.en: a round part of a vehicle that turns and lets it move

examples.en: The car has four wheels.
One wheel of the cart is broken.
examples.cn: 手推车的一个轮子坏了。

wheel.etymology: 源自古英语 hweol,与希腊语 kyklos(圆)同源。

definitions.en: a long thin piece of leather used to hit animals

examples.en: The man held a whip in his hand.
examples.cn: 那个人手里拿着一根鞭子。

examples.en: He used a whip to drive the horse.

whip.etymology: 源自中古英语 whippen,意为快速抽动。

definitions.en: a small object that makes a high sound when you blow it

examples.en: The teacher blew her whistle.
I heard the whistle of the train.
examples.cn: 我听到了火车的汽笛声。

whistle.etymology: 源自古英语 hwistlian,拟声词,模仿吹哨声。

definitions.en: an opening in a wall with glass that lets in light and air

examples.en: Please open the window.
A bird flew past the window.

window.etymology: 源自古诺尔斯语 vindauga,字面意为‘风眼’(wind-eye)。

definitions.en: the part of a bird or plane used for flying

examples.en: The bird opened its wings.
The plane's wing is very long.

wing.etymology: 源自古诺尔斯语 vængr,意为翅。

definitions.en: a thin thread of metal used to carry electricity or tie things

examples.en: The wire carries electricity to the house.
examples.cn: 这根电线把电送到房子里。

examples.en: He tied the box with a wire.
examples.cn: 他用金属丝把箱子捆好。

wire.etymology: 源自古英语 wir,意为细金属丝。

definitions.en: a small thin animal with a soft body and no legs

examples.en: A worm came out of the wet earth.
examples.cn: 一条虫子从湿土里钻了出来。

examples.en: Birds eat worms.

worm.etymology: 源自古英语 wyrm,意为蛇、虫。

definitions.cn: 有能力做某事的；能干的
definitions.en: having the power or skill to do something

examples.en: She is able to run very fast.
He is an able worker.

able.etymology: 源自拉丁语 habilis（容易拿住的、合适的），经古法语进入英语。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调具备完成特定任务的素质

definitions.en: having a sour, sharp taste

examples.en: The drink had an acid taste.
Lemons are acid fruits.

acid.etymology: 源自拉丁语 acidus（酸的），与 acer（尖锐的）同源。

synonyms.nuance: 更口语，常指食物变质的酸

definitions.en: feeling or showing strong displeasure

examples.en: He was angry with his friend.
Her angry words hurt me.

angry.etymology: 源自古诺尔斯语 angr（悲伤、苦恼），加形容词后缀 -y。

synonyms.nuance: 更口语，多用于美式英语

definitions.en: working by itself without human control

examples.en: The door is automatic.
This car has an automatic system.

automatic.etymology: 源自希腊语 automatos（自行运作的），auto-（自己）+ -matos（思考、意愿）。

definitions.en: very pleasing to look at or hear

examples.en: She has a beautiful smile.
The garden looks beautiful in spring.

beautiful.etymology: 由 beauty（美）+ 后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成。

synonyms.nuance: 程度较轻，多用于女性或小物

definitions.en: of the darkest color, like night

examples.en: She wore a black dress.
The cat is black.

black.etymology: 源自古英语 blæc（黑色的、墨色的）。

synonyms.nuance: 泛指缺乏光线，不一定是纯黑

definitions.en: very hot, bubbling like water over heat

examples.en: Pour the boiling water into the cup.
It was a boiling hot day.

boiling.etymology: 由动词 boil（煮沸，源自拉丁语 bullire 起泡）加 -ing 构成。

definitions.en: giving out or filled with much light

examples.en: The sun is very bright today.
She likes bright colors.

bright.etymology: 源自古英语 beorht（明亮的、闪耀的）。

definitions.en: in pieces or not working

examples.en: The glass is broken.
He fixed the broken chair.

broken.etymology: 动词 break（折断，源自古英语 brecan）的过去分词。

synonyms.nuance: 泛指受到损害，不一定碎裂

definitions.en: of the color of earth or wood

examples.en: He has brown eyes.
The bread is brown.

brown.etymology: 源自古英语 brun（棕色的、暗色的）。

definitions.en: costing little money

examples.en: This shirt is very cheap.
We found a cheap hotel.
examples.cn: 我们找到一家便宜的旅馆。

cheap.etymology: 源自古英语 cēap（买卖、价格），后缩略为表示价格低廉。

synonyms.nuance: 更中性，无廉价质差的含义

definitions.en: relating to chemistry or chemicals

examples.en: There was a chemical change in the water.
The factory uses many chemical products.
examples.cn: 工厂使用许多化学产品。

chemical.etymology: 由 chemic（炼金术的，源自 alchemy）加 -al 构成。

definitions.en: most important; highest in rank

examples.en: Health is our chief concern.
examples.cn: 健康是我们的首要关切。

examples.en: Rice is the chief food here.

chief.etymology: 源自古法语 chief（头、首领），来自拉丁语 caput（头）。

definitions.en: free from dirt or marks

examples.en: Please keep your hands clean.
The room is clean and bright.

clean.etymology: 源自古英语 clǣne（纯净的、干净的）。

definitions.en: easy to see, hear, or understand

examples.en: The sky is clear today.
Her voice was loud and clear.

clear.etymology: 源自古法语 cler，来自拉丁语 clarus（明亮的、清楚的）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调简单易懂、毫不含糊

definitions.en: happening often; shared by many

examples.en: Colds are common in winter.
We have a common goal.
examples.cn: 我们有一个共同的目标。

common.etymology: 源自古法语 comun，来自拉丁语 communis（共有的）。

definitions.cn: 复杂的；由许多部分组成的
definitions.en: made of many connected parts; not simple

examples.en: This is a complex problem.
The machine has a complex design.

complex.etymology: 源自拉丁语 complexus（缠绕在一起的），com-（一起）+ plectere（编织）。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调难以处理、令人困惑

definitions.en: awake and aware of things around you

examples.en: He was still conscious after the fall.
She is conscious of the danger.

conscious.etymology: 源自拉丁语 conscius（知情的），com-（一起）+ scire（知道）。

synonyms.nuance: 更常用，强调注意到某事

definitions.en: divided or shaped by a sharp edge

examples.en: She put the cut flowers in a vase.
examples.cn: 她把剪下的花插进花瓶。

examples.en: He cleaned the cut bread.

cut.etymology: 源自中古英语 cutten（切割），词源不甚明确。

definitions.cn: 深的；从表面到底部距离大的
definitions.en: going far down from the top or surface

examples.en: The river is very deep here.
She took a deep breath.

synonyms.nuance: 多用于抽象意义，如思想深刻

definitions.en: needing someone or something for support

examples.en: A baby is dependent on its mother.
Our plan is dependent on the weather.
examples.cn: 我们的计划取决于天气。

dependent.etymology: 源自拉丁语 dependere（悬挂、依靠），de-（向下）+ pendere（悬挂）。

definitions.en: happening before the usual or expected time

examples.en: We had an early breakfast.
She caught the early train.

early.etymology: 源自古英语 ǣrlīce（在……之前），由 ǣr（早）构成。

synonyms.nuance: 强调时机未到、提前过头

definitions.en: able to stretch and return to its shape

examples.en: The band is very elastic.
Rubber is an elastic material.

elastic.etymology: 源自希腊语 elastikos（有推动力的），与 elaunein（驱动）相关。

definitions.en: worked by or producing electricity

examples.en: She bought an electric light.
This is an electric car.

electric.etymology: 源自拉丁语 electrum（琥珀），因摩擦琥珀生电而得名。

definitions.en: the same in size, number, or value

examples.en: Cut the cake into equal parts.
examples.cn: 把蛋糕切成相等的几块。

examples.en: All people are equal.

equal.etymology: 源自拉丁语 aequalis（相等的），来自 aequus（平的、公正的）。

definitions.en: having a lot of flesh on the body

examples.en: The cat is too fat.
He ate a lot and got fat.

fat.etymology: 源自古英语 fǣtt（肥的、油腻的）。

definitions.en: able to produce many plants or young

examples.en: The land here is very fertile.
Fertile soil grows good crops.
examples.cn: 肥沃的土壤长出好庄稼。

fertile.etymology: 源自拉丁语 fertilis（多产的），来自 ferre（带来、生产）。

synonyms.nuance: 泛指产出高，不限于土地

definitions.en: coming before all others in order or time

examples.en: She won first prize.
This is my first day at work.

first.etymology: 源自古英语 fyrst（最前的），是 fore（前）的最高级形式。

definitions.en: fastened in place; not changing

examples.en: The shelf is fixed to the wall.
We meet at a fixed time.
examples.cn: 我们在固定的时间见面。

fixed.etymology: 动词 fix（固定，源自拉丁语 fixus）的过去分词。

definitions.en: smooth and level, without bumps

examples.en: The road is long and flat.
Put the paper on a flat surface.
examples.cn: 把纸放在平整的表面上。

flat.etymology: 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr（平的）。

definitions.en: not controlled or limited; costing nothing

examples.en: The birds are free to fly.
The tickets are free.

free.etymology: 源自古英语 frēo（自由的、不受束缚的）。

definitions.en: happening often

examples.en: He is a frequent visitor here.
There are frequent buses to town.
examples.cn: 去镇上的公交车很频繁。

frequent.etymology: 源自拉丁语 frequens（拥挤的、频繁的）。

definitions.en: holding as much as possible

examples.en: The cup is full of water.
The bus was full.

synonyms.nuance: 强调被装满的动作结果

definitions.en: relating to most people or things; not detailed

examples.en: This is the general opinion.
He gave us a general idea of the plan.
examples.cn: 他给我们讲了计划的大致情况。

general.etymology: 源自拉丁语 generalis（属于全体的），来自 genus（种类）。

examples.en: Good morning, everyone!

definitions.en: very large, important, or good

examples.en: He is a great leader.
There was a great noise outside.

great.etymology: 源自古英语 grēat（大的、粗的）。

synonyms.nuance: 只指尺寸大，不含伟大之意

definitions.en: of a color between black and white

examples.en: The sky is grey before rain.
He has grey hair.

grey.etymology: 源自古英语 grǣg（灰色的）；美式英语常拼作 gray。

definitions.en: fixed at the top and hanging down freely

examples.en: She loves the hanging lamp.
There were hanging plants by the window.

hanging.etymology: 由动词 hang（悬挂，源自古英语 hangian）加 -ing 构成。

synonyms.nuance: 较书面，强调被吊在空中

definitions.en: feeling or showing pleasure

examples.en: The children look happy.
I am happy to see you.

happy.etymology: 由 hap（运气，源自古诺尔斯语 happ）加 -y 构成，本义为幸运的。

definitions.en: firm and solid; difficult to do

examples.en: The stone is very hard.
It was a hard question.

hard.etymology: 源自古英语 heard（坚硬的、严酷的）。

synonyms.nuance: 仅指难度，不指物理硬度

definitions.en: in good health; good for the body

examples.en: She is a healthy child.
We should eat healthy food.
examples.cn: 我们应该吃健康的食物。

healthy.etymology: 由 health（健康，源自古英语 hǣlth）加 -y 构成。

synonyms.nuance: 多作表语，指当下没生病

definitions.en: rising far above the ground or others

examples.en: The wall is too high.
Birds fly high in the sky.

synonyms.nuance: 多形容人或细长物体的身高

definitions.en: having an empty space inside

examples.en: The tube is hollow.
Birds make nests in hollow trees.

hollow.etymology: 源自古英语 holh（洞、凹处）。

definitions.en: of great value or meaning

examples.en: This is an important day.
Sleep is important for health.

important.etymology: 源自拉丁语 importare（带入、关系重大），in-（向内）+ portare（携带）。

definitions.en: friendly and caring toward others

examples.en: She is kind to everyone.
Thank you for your kind help.

kind.etymology: 源自古英语 gecynde（天生的、本性的），后引申为善良。

definitions.en: having the same qualities; similar

examples.en: The two boys are of like age.
They reacted in like manner.
examples.cn: 他们以同样的方式作出反应。

like.etymology: 源自古英语 gelīc（相似的）。

definitions.en: alive; not dead

examples.en: Fish are living things.
He is the greatest living artist.
examples.cn: 他是当今在世的最伟大的艺术家。

living.etymology: 由动词 live（活，源自古英语 libban）加 -ing 构成。

definitions.en: having great length in space or time

examples.en: She has long hair.
It was a long day.

definitions.en: of the sex that does not give birth

examples.en: A male lion has a mane.
Most workers here are male.
examples.cn: 这里大多数工人是男性。

male.etymology: 源自拉丁语 masculus（男性的）的小词形式，经古法语进入英语。

synonyms.nuance: 多指男性气质或语法阳性

definitions.en: having a husband or wife

examples.en: They are happily married.
She is a married woman.

married.etymology: 动词 marry（结婚，源自拉丁语 maritare）的过去分词。

definitions.en: relating to physical things rather than ideas

examples.en: They care too much about material things.
examples.cn: 他们太看重物质的东西。

examples.en: The material world is full of change.

material.etymology: 源自拉丁语 materialis，来自 materia（物质、材料）。

definitions.en: relating to medicine or the treatment of illness

examples.en: She needs medical help right now.
He went to medical school for many years.

medical.etymology: 源自拉丁语 medicus（医生），来自 medeor（治疗）。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调实际治疗与诊断的场景

definitions.en: relating to soldiers, armies, or war

examples.en: The country has a strong military force.
examples.cn: 这个国家有强大的军事力量。

examples.en: He joined the military training program.
examples.cn: 他参加了军事训练项目。

military.etymology: 源自拉丁语 militaris，来自 miles（士兵）。

synonyms.nuance: 偏书面，常用于固定搭配如 martial law

definitions.cn: 由自然产生而非人造的
definitions.en: existing in nature and not made by people
normal and to be expected

examples.en: This soap is made from natural things.
examples.cn: 这块肥皂由天然原料制成。

examples.en: It is natural to feel sad sometimes.
examples.cn: 有时感到难过是很自然的。

natural.etymology: 源自拉丁语 naturalis，来自 natura（自然、本性）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调不含杂质，未必指天然来源

definitions.en: needed in order to do or achieve something

examples.en: Sleep is necessary for good health.
Take all the necessary tools with you.

necessary.etymology: 源自拉丁语 necessarius，来自 necesse（不可避免的、必需的）。

synonyms.nuance: 语气更强，指构成核心、绝对不可缺

definitions.en: recently made, bought, or come into being

examples.en: She bought a new car last week.
We have a new student in our class.
examples.cn: 我们班来了一名新同学。

new.etymology: 源自古英语 nīwe，与德语 neu 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 强调刚出现、未被使用，常带活力感

definitions.en: usual, typical, or expected

examples.en: It is normal to feel tired after work.
examples.cn: 下班后感到累是正常的。

examples.en: His temperature is back to normal.

normal.etymology: 源自拉丁语 normalis（依照直角的），来自 norma（标准、规则）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调常见、习以为常，而非合乎标准

definitions.cn: 没有关闭的、能进入或通过的
definitions.en: not closed, allowing things to pass through

examples.en: The door is open, please come in.
The shop is open until late.
examples.cn: 这家店一直营业到很晚。

open.etymology: 源自古英语 open，与 up 相关，本义为“向上掀开的”。

synonyms.nuance: 特指锁没锁上，不一定门是开着的

definitions.cn: 两条线等距且永不相交的
definitions.en: of lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet

examples.en: The two roads run parallel to each other.
Draw two parallel lines on the page.

parallel.etymology: 源自希腊语 parallēlos，由 para（旁边）+ allēlōn（彼此）构成。

synonyms.nuance: 强调排成一线，不一定数学意义上平行

definitions.en: having already happened or ended

examples.en: We talked about the past week.
examples.cn: 我们谈起了过去的一周。

examples.en: Those troubles are all in the past.

past.etymology: 由动词 pass 的过去分词演变而来。

synonyms.nuance: 强调在某事之前，相对而言更具体

definitions.en: relating to the body rather than the mind
relating to material things or the science of physics

examples.en: Running is good physical exercise.
examples.cn: 跑步是很好的身体锻炼。

examples.en: The room has no physical barriers.
examples.cn: 这个房间没有任何实体障碍。

physical.etymology: 源自希腊语 physis（自然），经拉丁语 physicalis 进入英语。

synonyms.nuance: 专指与肉体相关，不涉及物理学含义

definitions.en: relating to the government or public affairs of a country

examples.en: They held a political meeting today.
examples.cn: 他们今天举行了一场政治会议。

examples.en: She has strong political views.

political.etymology: 源自希腊语 politikos（关于公民、国家的），来自 polis（城邦）。

synonyms.nuance: 特指与政府机构有关，范围比政治窄

antonyms.cn: 非政治的；不关心政治的

nodes.label: apolitical
nodes.cn: 非政治的；不关心政治的

definitions.en: having little money or few possessions
of low quality or below the expected level

examples.en: The poor family had little food.
examples.cn: 这个贫穷的家庭几乎没有食物。

examples.en: His work is of poor quality.

poor.etymology: 源自古法语 povre，来自拉丁语 pauper（贫穷的）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调因贫穷而急需帮助

definitions.en: able to be done or to happen

examples.en: Is it possible to finish today?
Please come as soon as possible.

possible.etymology: 源自拉丁语 possibilis，来自 posse（能够）。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调实际可操作、行得通

definitions.en: existing or happening now
being in a particular place

examples.en: All the students were present today.
The present time is hard for many.
examples.cn: 当前对许多人来说很艰难。

present.etymology: 源自拉丁语 praesens，由 prae（在前）+ esse（存在）构成。

synonyms.nuance: 强调此刻正在进行、最新的

definitions.en: belonging to one person, not for public use

examples.en: This is my private room.
They had a private talk.
examples.cn: 他们进行了一次私下交谈。

private.etymology: 源自拉丁语 privatus（独属个人的），来自 privare（剥离、分开）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调与个人相关，不一定排斥他人

definitions.cn: 很有可能发生或为真的
definitions.en: likely to happen or to be true

examples.en: Rain is probable this afternoon.
It is the most probable answer.

probable.etymology: 源自拉丁语 probabilis（可证明的、可信的），来自 probare（证明、检验）。

synonyms.nuance: 更口语、更常用，语气略弱

definitions.cn: 用时很短的、动作迅速的
definitions.en: moving or done with speed; taking little time

examples.en: She gave a quick answer.
Let's take a quick look.

quick.etymology: 源自古英语 cwic（活着的、有生命的），后引申为“迅速的”。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调持续的高速度，quick 偏短促即时

definitions.cn: 没有或几乎没有声音的
definitions.en: making little or no noise

examples.en: The library is very quiet.
Please be quiet in here.

quiet.etymology: 源自拉丁语 quietus（平静的、安息的），来自 quies（休息）。

synonyms.nuance: 语气更强，指完全没有声音

definitions.cn: 已做好准备可以行动的
definitions.en: fully prepared to do something

examples.en: Are you ready to go?
Dinner is ready now.

ready.etymology: 源自古英语 rǣde（准备好的、骑行的），与 ride 相关。

synonyms.nuance: 更正式，强调事先做过准备

definitions.en: having the colour of blood or fire

examples.en: She wore a red dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条红色的裙子。

examples.en: The apple is bright red.

red.etymology: 源自古英语 rēad，与拉丁语 ruber、希腊语 erythros 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 指鲜艳的亮红色，更具体

definitions.cn: 按固定间隔反复发生的
definitions.en: happening at the same time or in the same way each time

examples.en: He takes regular walks every day.
She is a regular visitor here.

regular.etymology: 源自拉丁语 regularis（依规则的），来自 regula（尺、规则）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调持续不变，不一定按固定间隔

definitions.en: having the duty to deal with or take care of something

examples.en: She is responsible for the team.
He is a responsible young man.
examples.cn: 他是个有责任心的年轻人。

responsible.etymology: 源自拉丁语 responsus（回应），来自 respondere（回答、负责）。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调需对结果作出交代

definitions.en: correct or true
on or toward the right side

examples.en: You gave the right answer.
Turn to the right side.

right.etymology: 源自古英语 riht（直的、正确的），与拉丁语 rectus 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 更正式，强调符合事实或标准

definitions.en: shaped like a circle or a ball

examples.en: The table is round.
She drew a round shape.

round.etymology: 源自古法语 roont，来自拉丁语 rotundus（圆的），与 rota（轮子）相关。

synonyms.nuance: 更书面，专指平面上的圆

definitions.en: exactly alike; not different

examples.en: We have the same idea.
They live in the same town.

same.etymology: 源自古诺斯语 samr，与拉丁语 similis（相似的）同源。

synonyms.nuance: 语气更强，强调毫无差别

definitions.en: coming after the first in order

examples.en: This is my second try.
She came in second place.

second.etymology: 源自拉丁语 secundus（跟随的、第二的），来自 sequi（跟随）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调顺序上紧随其后，不一定是第二

definitions.en: not joined or connected; apart

examples.en: They sleep in separate rooms.
Keep these two things separate.

separate.etymology: 源自拉丁语 separatus，由 se-（分开）+ parare（准备、安排）构成。

synonyms.nuance: 强调彼此明显有别，而非物理分离

definitions.en: thoughtful and not joking
bad or dangerous enough to worry about

examples.en: He gave me a serious look.
This is a serious problem.

serious.etymology: 源自拉丁语 serius（庄重的、认真的）。

synonyms.nuance: 更书面，常用于危急或令人忧虑的情形

definitions.cn: 有能切割或刺穿的利刃或尖端的
definitions.en: having a thin edge or point that can cut or pierce

examples.en: Be careful, the knife is sharp.
The pencil has a sharp point.

sharp.etymology: 源自古英语 scearp（锋利的），与德语 scharf 同源。

definitions.cn: 表面平整、摸起来不粗糙的
definitions.en: having an even surface; not rough

examples.en: The stone feels smooth.
examples.cn: 这块石头摸起来很光滑。

examples.en: She has smooth skin.

smooth.etymology: 源自古英语 smōth，本义即“平滑的”。

definitions.en: tending to stick to things; covered with something that sticks

examples.en: My hands are sticky from the candy.
examples.cn: 我的手被糖弄得黏糊糊的。

examples.en: The tape is very sticky.

sticky.etymology: 由 stick（粘附）+ 形容词后缀 -y 构成。

definitions.en: firm and difficult to bend or move

examples.en: The card is stiff and hard.
My neck feels stiff today.

stiff.etymology: 源自古英语 stīf（坚硬的、不弯的），与德语 steif 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 更正式，强调完全不能弯折

definitions.en: going in one direction without bending or curving

examples.en: Draw a straight line here.
The road is long and straight.

straight.etymology: 源自中古英语 streght，为 stretch（拉伸）的过去分词形式。

synonyms.nuance: 强调路线不绕弯，也用于抽象意义

definitions.en: having great power, force, or physical strength

examples.en: He is strong enough to lift it.
examples.cn: 他力气够大，能把它举起来。

examples.en: She has a strong arm.

strong.etymology: 源自古英语 strang（有力的），与德语 streng 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调影响力或机械力量

definitions.cn: 出乎意料地很快发生的
definitions.en: happening quickly and unexpectedly

examples.en: There was a sudden noise.
His sudden visit surprised us.
examples.cn: 他突然来访让我们很意外。

sudden.etymology: 源自古法语 sodain，来自拉丁语 subitaneus（突然的），由 subire（悄然到来）演变。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调出乎意料、缺乏过渡，带生硬感

definitions.en: having a taste like sugar

examples.en: This cake is very sweet.
The fruit tastes sweet.

sweet.etymology: 源自古英语 swēte，与拉丁语 suavis、希腊语 hēdys 同源。

definitions.en: of more than average height

examples.en: He is the tallest in the class.
There is a tall tree by the road.

tall.etymology: 源自古英语 getæl（迅速的、得体的），中古英语后转为“高的”。

synonyms.nuance: 多指物体离地高，tall 多指物体本身从底到顶长

definitions.en: having a large distance between opposite surfaces
of a liquid that does not flow easily

examples.en: The wall is very thick.
She made a thick soup.

thick.etymology: 源自古英语 þicce（厚的、密的），与德语 dick 同源。

definitions.cn: 拉得很紧或贴得很牢的
definitions.en: fixed firmly in place or fitting closely

examples.en: These shoes are too tight.
Make sure the rope is tight.

tight.etymology: 源自中古英语 tight（密的、紧的），与古诺斯语 þéttr 相关。

synonyms.nuance: 强调稳固不松动，不一定指贴身

definitions.en: needing rest or sleep; weary

examples.en: I am very tired tonight.
She looked tired after work.
examples.cn: 下班后她看起来很疲倦。

tired.etymology: 由动词 tire（使疲劳，古英语 tēorian）加 -ed 构成。

synonyms.nuance: 更书面，常含长期劳累或厌倦之意

definitions.en: in accordance with fact; not false

examples.en: The story is true.
Is it true that you are leaving?

true.etymology: 源自古英语 trēowe（忠实的、可信的），与 trust 相关。

synonyms.nuance: 强调没有错误，true 强调符合事实

definitions.cn: 使用或带有强烈破坏力量的
definitions.en: using or involving great physical force, often to hurt or damage

examples.en: There was a violent storm last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚有一场猛烈的暴风雨。

examples.en: He has a violent temper.

violent.etymology: 源自拉丁语 violentus，来自 vis（力量）。

synonyms.nuance: 强调猛烈、激烈，未必涉及伤害

definitions.en: staying in a place until something happens or someone comes

examples.en: Many people sat in the waiting room.
There is a long waiting line.
examples.cn: 有一条长长的等候队伍。

waiting.etymology: 由动词 wait（等待，源自古法语 waitier）加 -ing 构成。

synonyms.nuance: 更书面，指事情有待处理或决定

definitions.en: of a fairly high temperature; pleasantly hot

examples.en: The water is nice and warm.
Wear a warm coat today.

warm.etymology: 源自古英语 wearm（温暖的），与德语 warm 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 多指天气不冷不热、气候宜人

definitions.cn: 被水或其他液体覆盖或浸透的
definitions.en: covered or soaked with water or another liquid

examples.en: My clothes are all wet.
The grass is wet in the morning.

wet.etymology: 源自古英语 wǣt（湿的），与 water 相关。

synonyms.nuance: 指略微湿润，程度比 wet 轻

definitions.cn: 从一边到另一边距离大的
definitions.en: measuring a large distance from one side to the other

examples.en: This is a wide river.
The road is very wide here.

wide.etymology: 源自古英语 wīd（宽阔的、远的），与德语 weit 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 更强调表面的辽阔感，常用于肩膀、平原等

definitions.cn: 有良好判断力和知识的
definitions.en: having or showing good sense and judgement

examples.en: She made a wise choice.
examples.cn: 她做了一个明智的选择。

examples.en: He is a wise old man.

wise.etymology: 源自古英语 wīs（聪明的、博学的），与 wit 相关。

synonyms.nuance: 强调讲求实际、判断稳妥，不强调深厚智慧

definitions.cn: 像柠檬或金子一样颜色的
definitions.en: having the colour of a lemon or gold

examples.en: The sun looks yellow.
She picked a yellow flower.

yellow.etymology: 源自古英语 geolu（黄色的），与德语 gelb 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 指带光泽的金色黄，更鲜亮

definitions.cn: 活了或存在时间不长的
definitions.en: having lived or existed for only a short time

examples.en: She is a young girl.
The tree is still young.

young.etymology: 源自古英语 geong（年轻的），与德语 jung、拉丁语 juvenis 同源。

synonyms.nuance: 强调具有年轻人的活力与特质

definitions.en: not asleep

examples.en: She is still awake.
I lay awake all night.

awake.etymology: 源自古英语 awæcnan，由前缀 a-（出）+ wake（醒）构成。

synonyms.nuance: 不仅醒着，还强调注意力集中、机敏

definitions.en: not good; of poor quality

examples.en: The weather was bad all week.
He made a bad choice.
examples.cn: 他做了一个糟糕的选择。

bad.etymology: 源自古英语 bæddel，意为坏的、低劣的。

synonyms.nuance: 强调质量或水平不达标

definitions.en: not straight; curved or angled

examples.en: The old nail was bent.
She picked up the bent wire.
examples.cn: 她捡起那根弯曲的铁丝。

bent.etymology: 源自动词 bend（弯）的过去分词。

definitions.en: having a sharp, unpleasant taste
causing or feeling deep pain or resentment

examples.en: This coffee is too bitter.
She felt bitter about the loss.
examples.cn: 她对这次失败感到痛苦。

bitter.etymology: 源自古英语 biter，与 bite（咬）同源，意为刺痛的。

definitions.en: having the color of a clear sky

examples.en: The sky is blue today.
She wore a blue dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条蓝色的裙子。

blue.etymology: 源自古法语 bleu，意为蓝色。

definitions.en: sure; without doubt
particular but not named

examples.en: I am certain he will come.
A certain man asked for you.

certain.etymology: 源自拉丁语 certus，意为已定的、确定的。

definitions.en: of low temperature

examples.en: The water is very cold.
It gets cold at night.

cold.etymology: 源自古英语 cald，意为寒冷的。

definitions.en: having all the necessary parts
total; to the fullest degree

examples.en: The set is now complete.
It was a complete surprise.

complete.etymology: 源自拉丁语 completus，complere（填满）的过去分词。

definitions.en: causing pain and showing no kindness

examples.en: It was cruel to leave the dog alone.
examples.cn: 把狗单独留下太残忍了。

examples.en: He gave a cruel laugh.

cruel.etymology: 源自拉丁语 crudelis，意为粗暴的、残酷的。

definitions.en: with little or no light
of a deep, not light shade

examples.en: The room was dark and quiet.
She has dark hair.

dark.etymology: 源自古英语 deorc，意为黑暗的。

definitions.en: no longer alive

examples.en: The plant is dead.
We found a dead bird.

dead.etymology: 源自古英语 dēad，意为死的。

synonyms.nuance: 更书面，也可形容缺乏生气

definitions.en: much loved; precious
costing a lot of money

examples.en: She is a dear friend.
Meat is very dear here.

dear.etymology: 源自古英语 dēore，意为珍贵的、心爱的。

synonyms.nuance: 专指价格高，不含情感义

definitions.en: finely made and easily damaged
easily broken or harmed

examples.en: The glass is very delicate.
She has delicate skin.

delicate.etymology: 源自拉丁语 delicatus，意为精致的、可爱的。

definitions.en: not the same as another

examples.en: These two books are different.
He looks different now.
examples.cn: 他现在看起来不一样了。

different.etymology: 源自拉丁语 differre（分开、相异）。

definitions.en: not clean; covered with dirt

examples.en: His hands were dirty.
Please wash the dirty plates.

dirty.etymology: 源自中古英语 dirt（污物）加形容词后缀 -y。

definitions.en: without water or moisture

examples.en: The towel is dry now.
We need dry wood for the fire.
examples.cn: 我们需要干木头来生火。

dry.etymology: 源自古英语 drȳge，意为干的。

definitions.en: not true or correct
not real; made to deceive

examples.en: His answer was false.
She wore a false beard.

false.etymology: 源自拉丁语 falsus（fallere 欺骗的过去分词）。

definitions.en: lacking strength; weak

examples.en: The old man was feeble.
She gave a feeble smile.

feeble.etymology: 源自拉丁语 flebilis，意为可悲的、令人哭泣的。

definitions.en: of the sex that can have babies or lay eggs

examples.en: A female bird built the nest.
The school has many female teachers.
examples.cn: 这所学校有很多女教师。

female.etymology: 源自拉丁语 femella（女性的小词），后受 male 影响拼写。

definitions.en: lacking good sense; silly

examples.en: It was foolish to go out in the storm.
examples.cn: 在暴风雨中出门是愚蠢的。

examples.en: Don't make a foolish mistake.

foolish.etymology: 源自 fool（傻瓜）加形容词后缀 -ish。

definitions.en: happening or existing in the time to come

examples.en: We must plan for future needs.
examples.cn: 我们必须为未来的需求做计划。

examples.en: This is his future home.

future.etymology: 源自拉丁语 futurus，be（成为）的将来分词。

definitions.en: having the color of grass

examples.en: The grass is green.
She painted the door green.

green.etymology: 源自古英语 grēne，与 grow（生长）同源。

definitions.en: not in good health; sick

examples.en: She felt ill after lunch.
He has been ill for a week.

ill.etymology: 源自古诺斯语 illr，意为坏的。

definitions.en: coming after all others
most recent before now

examples.en: December is the last month.
I saw her last week.

last.etymology: 源自古英语 latost，late（晚）的最高级。

definitions.en: after the expected or usual time

examples.en: He was late for the meeting.
